blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Each inspection takes 45 minutes on site. A planner's time callback returns only drive minutes, and the plan shows one crew reaching six sites by 10:00. What should the model change?

options.text: Add 45 minutes per site to the arc cost, so the objective counts the work
options.says: The arc cost is the objective; arrival times come from the time dimension, which would still skip the work.

options.text: Add each site's 45 minutes to the time transit of the arc that leaves it
options.says: Right: transit(a to b) = service at a + travel from a to b, so the next arrival comes after the work.

options.text: Allow 45 minutes of slack at each site, so the crew always stops there
options.says: Slack is waiting the solver may use, from 0 up to its bound; it never forces time to pass.

options.text: Nothing, since the arrival windows already leave room for the work
options.says: The lesson's travel-only plan, replayed with real inspections, missed two windows.

origin.section: Time Is a Dimension Whose Transit Is Service Plus Travel

questions.stem: A routing plan prints one stop as B 09:20-09:50, from solution.Min and solution.Max of B's time cumul. What does it say about the crew's arrival at B?

options.text: It arrives at 09:20 and works on site at B until 09:50
options.says: Both times are arrival times; the work at B is in the transit of the arc that leaves B.

options.text: It must arrive at 09:50, since that is when B's own window closes
options.says: The range lies inside B's window but need not end where the window does, and it is not one time.

options.text: Arriving any time from 09:20 to 09:50 keeps the route feasible
options.says: Right: the cumul's minimum and maximum in the solution are the solution window.

options.text: It waits 30 minutes at B, the slack that the solver chose there
options.says: The range is room to arrive, not a wait; the slack at B is a separate quantity.

origin.section: Each Stop Gets an Arrival Range, Not One Time

questions.stem: A time-window run with travel time as the arc cost and no service time prints Objective 140 and a total time of all routes of 163 minutes. Where do the other 23 minutes come from?

options.text: Waiting for windows to open: route times count it, arc costs do not
options.says: Right: the guide's example prints 71 and 82 for the same reason.

options.text: Penalties for dropped visits, which the objective takes off the total
options.says: There are no optional visits here, and a penalty adds to the objective, not subtracts.

options.text: Rounding, since the objective cuts every arc down to whole minutes
options.says: Travel times are integers already; nothing is rounded.

options.text: Slack left over, since the finalizer never sets the end times
options.says: AddVariableMinimizedByFinalizer sets each start and end time to its earliest feasible value.
